newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says Indonesia has no say on partner.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says Indonesia has no say on partner.

text.p: The Indonesian government does not have any sway over whom Bre-X Minerals Ltd chooses as a partner to develop its spectacular Busang gold discovery, a Bre-X spokesman said Friday.
"We feel we'll be free to pick our own partner," Steve McAnulty said in a phone interview from Calgary.
Bre-X has begun its search for a major partner to buy part or all of the Busang deposit, but the company has become embroiled in a dispute over the legal ownership of the site.
One of Bre-X's Indonesian partners is claiming up to 40 percent of Busang.
Bre-X has said the partner has a right to only 10 percent of part of the Bre-X property.
The Indonesian government has said it will delay approving the necessary contracts of work for Bre-X until the company can resolve its ownership dispute.
Analysts say the Indonesian government may withold the permits until it sees Bre-X's choice of partner.

In the past, the Indonesian government has held off issuing contracts of work for production until major companies are involved, said Roland Horst, the president of Minorca Resources Inc, which has an interest in Busang.
"There's always been a major in there before final contracts of work were given," he said in an interview.
But Bre-X said Friday it expects it will have resolved the ownership dispute and have the contracts of work in hand well before it is ready to announce a partner.
Bre-X and the Indonesian government have similar interests in finding a major gold producer to help develop the Busang property, said McAnulty.
"Obviously that partner will have to be of a certain stature," he said. "We both have the same objective there, both us and the Indonesian government."
Rumors that gold giant Barrick Gold Corp has sent high profile directors to Indonesia to speak with government officials are false, a Barrick spokesman said.
Barrick is interested in the deposit but Bre-X has to look after its contracts of work, Vince Borg told Reuters.
Interest from potential partners has not been dampened by the ownership dispute, said McAnulty of Bre-X.
But he said the process was still in its early stages and the company did not yet have any firm offers on the table.
Meanwhile, Bre-X president David Walsh and chief financial officer Rolando Francisco have been travelling for over a week to resolve the ownership issue, McAnulty said.
He would not say where they were or when they would be back, but they were confident they would reach a resolution "sooner rather than later."
Bre-X expects to have a new resource calculation and fresh drilling results in November, McAnulty said.
-- Heather Scoffield, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104
